motivation: Next-generation network switches and SDN controllers must enforce QoS policies (queuing, bandwidth reservation, routing priority) within the first few packets of a flow to avoid buffering delays and head-of-line blocking.

early_N_complete.description: Indicator of whether the flow reached at least N packets during its lifetime.

early_N_duration.description: Elapsed duration from flow start to the arrival of the N-th packet (or end of flow if total packets < N).

early_N_bytes.description: Cumulative bytes transmitted across both forward and backward directions in the first N packets.

early_N_fwd_pkts.description: Number of forward packets transmitted in the first N packets.

early_N_bwd_pkts.description: Number of backward packets transmitted in the first N packets.

early_N_avg_size.description: Average packet size across the first N packets (early_N_bytes / actual_early_pkts).

Early-5.operational_latency: Sub-millisecond to ~5ms. Ideal for immediate hardware QoS queue assignment.

Early-10.operational_latency: Low latency (~10-25ms). Captures initial TCP/TLS handshake negotiation.

Early-15.operational_latency: Medium latency (~25-50ms). Covers early post-handshake application exchange.

Full-Flow.features_description: Full 78 ML-safe behavioral features (excluding constant tcp_urg_count). Evaluated after flow completion.
Full-Flow.operational_latency: Post-flow (entire session duration). Used as the theoretical upper bound / performance ceiling.
